row.evidence: FortiCNAPP's admin guide says "SAML authentication supports Just-in-Time (JIT) user provisioning" to create a team member on first login; no SCIM endpoint is documented in the admin guide or API reference.
row.notes: New row. Lacework was acquired by Fortinet and is sold as Lacework FortiCNAPP; quote-only (fortinet.com product page offers 'Request a Quote'; lacework.com timed out to curl and the headless renderer). Users get in via SAML SSO with JIT (attributes map account-level admin/user/power-user roles and org roles) or FortiCloud IAM users; no SCIM, so JIT does not deprovision. Okta, Entra and Google setups use custom (non-catalogue) SAML apps; OneLogin has a FortiCNAPP catalogue app (SSO). REST API v2 exists (incl. audit logs) but its full reference sits behind the FNDN login. 'None' is by absence (rule 5).

plans.name: Lacework FortiCNAPP (quote-only)
plans.notes: No public tier table; pricing via Fortinet sales.

scim.notes: No SCIM endpoint in the FortiCNAPP Administration Guide (authentication section lists SAML SSO and SAML JIT pages per IdP only) or the API Reference PDF. 'false' is by absence (rule 5).

user_api.notes: The REST API v2 is public in outline, but the full endpoint reference lives on Fortinet's FNDN portal, which redirects to a login. No user/team-member endpoints are visible on public pages, so availability of a user-management API is left null.

okta.notes: No OIN result for 'lacework' or 'forticnapp'; vendor guide has admins create their own internal SAML app.

entra.notes: Vendor guide uses a non-gallery 'Create your own application' SAML app.

google.notes: Vendor guide uses a custom SAML app.

onelogin.notes: Per the vendor's OneLogin guide; provisioning is SAML JIT only.
